content: 1. For the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension, reduce the dose of sildenafil if it is being used for erectile dysfunction. 2. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir is contraindicated with silodosin as it increases silodosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to serious adverse effects. 3. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir is contraindicated with drugs highly dependent on CYP3A for clearance, where elevated concentrations can cause severe or life-threatening reactions. 4. Co-administration of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir with silodosin may increase the risk of postural hypotension. 5. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir is contraindicated with simvastatin due to increased levels of simvastatin via CYP3A4 inhibition. Discontinue simvastatin at least 12 hours before starting nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, during the 5-day treatment, and for 5 days after completing treatment. 6. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases the levels of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir by affecting CYP2B6 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 8. Co-administration of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir with sparsentan may increase toxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 9. St. John’s Wort decreases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to reduced efficacy and potential virologic failure. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir is contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inducers. 10. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases suvorexant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the tacrolimus dose by one-third and monitor for adverse effects such as neurotoxicity or QT prolongation. 12. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases tadalafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration if tadalafil is used for pulmonary arterial hypertension. Reduce the dose if used for erectile dysfunction. 13. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases tamsulosin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Pause tamsulosin and restart 3 days after completing nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 14. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases tenofovir AF levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for increased systemic exposure. 15. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ticagrelor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative antiplatelet agent, such as prasugrel, unless contraindicated. 16. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 17. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases tolvaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated due to the risk of dehydration, hypovolemia, and hyperkalemia. 18. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider lowering the trazodone dose and monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, dizziness, hypotension, and syncope. 19. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, leading to Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids such as beclomethasone or prednisolone. 20. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse effects. 21. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ubrogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse effects. 22. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases valsartan levels by inhibiting hepatic uptake transporters OATP1B1 and MRP2. No dosage modification is needed due to the short duration of treatment. 23. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases vamorolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. 24. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases vardenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Limit the dose to 5 mg every 72 hours. 25. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases venetoclax levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases venlafaxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential toxicity. 27. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases verapamil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for bradycardia, hypotension, or dizziness. Temporarily pause the antihypertensive drug if needed. 28. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases vinblastine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. 29. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases vincristine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for hematologic or gastrointestinal side effects. 30. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases voclosporin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This is contraindicated due to the risk of acute or chronic nephrotoxicity. 31. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases vorapaxar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases voriconazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 isoenzymes. Avoid co-administration. 33. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases voxilaprevir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases warfarin levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Monitor INR closely as it may increase or decrease. 35. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases zanubrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the dose to 80 mg once daily and resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 36. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases zidovudine levels by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases zuranolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the dose if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 38. Adverse effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir include dysgeusia (5%), diarrhea (3%), headache, hypertension, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and malaise. 39. Hypersensitivity reactions, including urticaria, angioedema, dyspnea, mild skin eruptions, pruritus, anaphylaxis, toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), and Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), have been reported. Discontinue immediately if significant hypersensitivity or anaphylaxis occurs and initiate appropriate treatment. 40. Hepatic transaminase elevations, clinical hepatitis, and jaundice have been reported with ritonavir. Use caution in patients with preexisting liver disease, liver enzyme abnormalities, or hepatitis. 41. Co-administration of nirmatrelvir with ritonavir may increase the risk of developing resistance to HIV protease inhibitors in individuals with uncontrolled or undiagnosed HIV-1 infection. 42. Breastfeeding individuals with COVID-19 should follow clinical guidelines to avoid exposing the infant to the virus. 43. Nirmatrelvir is a peptidomimetic inhibitor of the SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro), preventing viral replication by inhibiting polyprotein processing. 44. Ritonavir boosts nirmatrelvir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, increasing systemic exposure. 45. Nirmatrelvir must be co-administered with ritonavir to achieve therapeutic plasma levels. 46. Store nirmatrelvir/ritonavir at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with excursions permitted to 15–30°C (59–86°F). 47. Tablets should be swallowed whole and may be taken with or without food.
